requirements.summary: The live worker had the expected executable path and UID/GID 103/104, mapped to inventory-worker. The same identity, command, executable checksum, and healthy service state were observed after restart.

requirements.requirement: Limit the worker to at most 25 percent of one CPU.
requirements.summary: The worker's live cgroup reported cpu.max of 25000/100000. Saturated measurements before and after restart showed approximately 25% of one CPU with continuous throttling; the worker remained alive.

requirements.requirement: Limit the worker to 128 MiB of memory.
requirements.summary: The worker's live cgroup reported memory.max=134217728 bytes, exactly 128 MiB, both before and after restart. Post-restart usage was about 1.01 MiB.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct live-state and behavioral evidence. The mandatory restart protocol for the sole managed node is also complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were recorded, restart was acknowledged, connectivity dropped, a different boot identity was independently confirmed, and the service, executable, identity, limits, and load behavior recovered.
limitations: The lifecycle failed-services probe was unsupported because it used systemctl on Alpine; direct OpenRC status checks nevertheless showed both relevant services healthy.
Memory enforcement was verified through the live kernel memory.max control rather than by deliberately exhausting the full 128 MiB allowance.
Lifecycle snapshots are bounded and do not inventory every filesystem or OpenRC change, although the complete command audit and direct final probes cover the task-related mutations.
Requirement R1 cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-resource-worker

operational_hygiene.summary: The account creation, cgroup enablement, service/configuration creation, service enablement/start, and mandatory reboot were causally connected to the task or restart protocol. The only unnecessary mutation was the reboot command's creation of /tmp/inventory-worker-reboot.log; it remained after execution and was not cleaned up, but is low-risk residue. Package health was unchanged and no new listening service was exposed.
